object.name: evi.ringmod~
object.description: A clean FIR ring modulator algorithm with sine shaping saturation and filtering. Ring modulates two audio signals producing one modulated output, with antiderivative antialiasing and oversampling options.
object.discussion: The core linear algorithm is based on 'Enhanced Ring Mod' by Beat Frei. Copyright © 2008, 2009, 2010, Zurich University of the Arts, Beat Frei. GPL v2. See 'simpleRingmod()' in 'evi_ringmod_enhanced.genexpr' for more info.

inlets.description: The first audio signal to be ring modulated (Carrier).
The second audio signal to be ring modulated (Modulator).

outlets.digest: Ring Modulated Output but cool sounding
outlets.description: The audio result of the ring modulated inputs.

attributes.name: cutoff
attributes.description: The object offers a utility Butterworth Lowpass on it's output for taming the distortion and high frequencies. This is the cutoff frequency of that filter. By default the filter is bypassed. See the @order attribute for details.

attributes.name: drive
attributes.description: Drive the waveshaping input gain via a sine shaping function. A bit like a % 0..1.. up to 2 is pretty safe, up to 4 be careful (in terms of aliasing).

attributes.name: highpass
attributes.description: This applies a highpass to the initial ring modulated audio mix, for taming bass response. It is not smoothed and thus probably best used as a static tool only.

attributes.name: order
attributes.description: The object offers a utility Butterworth Lowpass on it's output for taming the distortion and high frequencies. 0 (the default) = bypassed (and CPU off), 1..8 = filter orders 1..8 (increasing in steepness of slope).

attributes.name: quality
attributes.description: 0=1x/Adaa1, 1=1x/Adaa2, 2=4x/Adaa2, 3=8x/Adaa2, 4=8x/Adaa2_4x. Because of the fake oversampling used here, higher and higher orders actually change the tonal effect of the audio output, so experimenting with different settings is not just about anti-aliasing or managing CPU usage but also a musical choice.

attributes.name: topology
attributes.description: The placement of the waveshaper in the ring modulator audio chain. If 0 (the default), the waveshaper sits after the ring modulator stage, if 1, the waveshaper is replaced into the middle of the ring modulator. Option 1 gives a strongly clipped and 'squeezed' guitar-like output. Option 0 gives a more usual soft saturated output.
